translations.text: The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, as Scripture says, and none of those who torment shall touch them in any way, since they have been cleansed of stains.
For these have risen above all these material and coarse things on the wings of the virtues, and, having reached the divine radiance, they shed light on everything under the sun.
Through their memory this visible, perceptible earth becomes bright as the dawn,
since, like great luminaries sending out brilliant rays, they make all who celebrate their memory shine, and they spread divine grace over the souls of the faithful,
who, with faith and longing, honour those who are written forever in the book of the living, with these humble yet most honourable gifts from us,
that is, words of praise, so honouring those who have become sharers in the divine glory.
Therefore, O faithful ones and lovers of the memory of the saints, it is fitting for us, as a kind of debt that cannot be avoided,
to give the saints praise and laudation as we celebrate their feast, so that through them we may receive good gifts in return.
For some of them gained heavenly crowns by their own blood, while others were anointed with the oil of the high priesthood and kept it holy,
unstained by any of the world's stains, and have stood in purity before the God of all, offering a sacrifice of praise with immaterial mouths.
Still others scorned all these bodily pleasures and tastes, wore down the body through fasting and constant prayer, and through all
kinds of hardship withered and weakened its tyranny. They are receiving from the Lord's right hand the rewards for their labours.
For in return for the pains and struggles they endured in this passing life, they have been granted brilliant gifts and the riches of incorruptible delights,
having been made dwellers in the mansions and delights of heaven. One of them is this blessed father of ours, the brilliant luminary John,
who, like a brilliant star, rose and shone on souls that had gone astray in the darkness of ignorance, and became their guide toward the light that knows no night.
For with the staff of faith he drove off the evil wolf, and, strengthened by the power of the Trinity, he kept his flock unharmed from its attacks.
This wonderful father of ours, worthy of remembrance and praised by all, sprang from the land of Mesopotamia.
Many writers, both those of ancient times and those who came after them, have praised this land highly for the abundance and cheapness of its fruits, its good air and its sweet waters,
for the rich growth of its plants, and even more for producing good and famous men.
Adorned above all by these men, it boasts of having gained such riches and glories.
So this blessed man took his earthly ancestry and homeland from the land mentioned above.
But the more exact place, the village that produced him, and the name it is called by are unknown to us.
Nor have we learned who his parents were or what their names were, who they were, or from whom they were descended.
But this alone has been handed down to us by those who wrote his life before us:
that he drew his bodily descent from the land of Mesopotamia, from a certain village lying near Antioch,
having received here the lot of his birth and upbringing, and having reached the fullness of age through learning and divine teachings.
But we know that his truest homeland is the Jerusalem above, and we are certain of it; and we have rightly learned that his father is the Creator of all,
the Father of this blessed father. For all of us were brought by him out of nothing into being and were fashioned by incorruptible hands,
so that we who seek incorruption may inherit immortal life and an unending kingdom in the mansions of the heavenly Father.
This blessed man, then, became learned through training in the divine Scriptures, and he richly stored up in his heart all the wealth of spiritual teachings.
And as he grew in age, a very great height of virtues was seen growing along with it in that man,
for he became winged in spirit, and he counted these earthly things, and the material things that drag one down to the earth, as altogether nothing.
So, having once put his hand to the plough that tills souls [?], he never turned back at all,
for he feared that a stone of stumbling might somewhere cut off his path toward the Kingdom and toward God.
When he had thus been made perfect in every kind of training and had gathered great wealth of learning for himself, he became zealous with zeal for the Lord and chose the monastic way of life.
And he did this while he was still young in years, yet aged and very sharp in understanding, for he had learned from the one who says: "I am alone until I pass away."

For this reason he chose to serve the One alone, in a single life, so that the eager service of the Lord would not be hindered by his being bound up with worldly cares through being yoked with a wife. Therefore,
saying "farewell" [literally "rejoice"] to the world and to all worldly things, he ran after the Lord, following in his footsteps, not weighed down by earthly possessions,
for day by day he stripped himself for the labours of the struggle, taking delight in fasting and vigil.
Such humility was seen in this godly man that he counted himself as altogether nothing, like the one who says: "I am a worm and not a man, and a reproach of men."
And what meekness he had! For he was entirely without anger, and in this he strove after the earth prepared for the meek to inherit.
He kept his anger only for the devil, the author of evils, since we are commanded to fight and stand against him alone, and not against men like ourselves.

Besides this, an unceasing fountain of tears always flowed from his eyes. Day and night he drenched his bed with tears and washed it with the stream running down from his eyes, according to the prophet who says:
And he would pray to the Lord to make him victorious over the tyranny of the flesh, which [35] drags the soul hard toward earthly and gross passions, especially in the age of youth,
since at that time the body serves as a ready instrument for the passions.
Thus, through constant prayer and supplication, he turned his enemies back utterly in shame,
For the Lord accepted his prayer, and he who raised up the victory carried off the trophies over his adversaries.
And, subduing the desires and passions of the flesh by wasting and constraining the body, he rose day by day toward the summit of the virtues.
And the grace of working miracles was granted to him by God, and he saw distant things as if they were near,
for with such graces God adorned his servant, he who does the will of those who fear him.
And through the performance of mighty works and miracles he made him shine like a brilliant star, radiant in soul and bright as the dawn in mind,
for those seized by various kinds of illness obtained a twofold healing through him,
since sight was granted to the blind and health to the sick, and to those tormented by the devil, freedom from his tyranny.
As such wonders were being accomplished by him, people came to him from every side to see him and to receive a blessing from him,
for the report of him spread through the whole land of Assyria because of the miracles and signs that had been granted to him by God.
When some time had passed in this way, it pleased the holy and venerable father John to depart from that place, for he fled from human glory,
which becomes very harmful to many, leads them astray from the way of God, and brings them down into the pit of perdition,
just as once, long ago, that boastful and arrogant one, who insolently vaunted that he would set his throne above the clouds, fell through his arrogance into the deepest darkness of hell.
He drove away this evil passion as one would expel some deadly poison.
And, raising spiritual wings, he fled into the desert for rest, together with some of his disciples,
so that, being free for divine things alone, he might keep his mind gathered for the practice and performance of the things that lighten the soul from these passions of the flesh.
So, having reached the desert and come upon a cave, he settled in it in quiet with his disciples, devoted to prayer and fasting and eager to fulfil all the divine commandments.
But the place remained hidden for a long time, and no one knew that the holy man had gone to those parts,
although many greatly longed to find the beloved father, the healer of souls and bodies; yet they were unable to reach the one they sought,
for his disciples would go secretly to the city and bring back food obtained by the work of their hands,
and, returning again secretly to their teacher, they made unceasing prayer and supplication to the Lord their occupation, like their teacher.
And with this would alternate handiwork, together with quiet speech of the tongue in thanksgiving to God,
so that the body should by no means be given rest through idleness of the hands, for they knew the saying of the Apostle: "These hands ministered to me and to those who were with me."
But God did not wish such a man to be hidden in obscurity, since "they do not light a lamp and put it under a bushel, but on a lampstand, so that it may give light to all."
For he revealed this saint of his to those who were seeking him and longing to find him, and the hidden treasure was given to those who desired to be enriched,
Since certain people, moved by a divine longing and searching in every way, were not deprived of their hope,
but obtained what they desired, God making his servant known for the benefit of many,
from then on a countless multitude again gathered to him, longing to hear his words and teachings.
And the sick, having found the physician, were brought to him carried on litters.
And those oppressed by demons and by all kinds of afflictions also hastened to this all-worthy father with eagerness and faith,
and so they obtained complete healing through the prayer of this saint, for all were granted freedom from their sufferings, and strength in place of weakness was swiftly granted to them.
And a multitude of signs and wonders were performed by this worthy father for those suffering from every kind of affliction; it is impossible to describe them one by one.
But since he fled from honors, and even more from the worldly disturbances that come with honor, he resolved to go away to foreign lands,
where no one would know him, so that in this way he might be able to live in solitude and stillness.
For this reason he said to his disciples who had followed him: "Brothers, if God wills, I intend to go away to foreign places,
so that in these few remaining days of my life I may live this sojourn and pilgrimage in the world with diligence and in solitude,
for, as we read, we are all strangers and passers-by, as our fathers also were.
But you, my beloved children, remain in this desert, on your guard against all the snares of the evil one, and pray to God for me as well,
that he may guide me in the paths pleasing to him and that my steps may not grow weak."
But when the disciples of the true teacher and instructor heard this word from the elder, they all answered with one voice:
"As the Lord lives and as your soul lives, we will never leave you alone; rather, we too will go with you
wherever you go, whether to life or to death, for we know you as our leader, who waters and nourishes our souls with the divine teachings
that come forth from your mouth, and through your prayers we hope to come to the good God."
When the blessed John saw his disciples bound to him by such love, he agreed that they should go with him wherever the Lord would lead them to the haven of his will.
And so, leaving his land and his homeland like another Abraham, called by the Lord's voice,
he came to the land of Kartli, to Mtskheta, the capital city, which at that time was foremost among the other cities.
And entering before the Life-giving Pillar, he worshipped the Lord together with his disciples,
falling down on the floor, soaking the ground with tears, and offering long supplications to the good and sweet King.
Now this venerable pillar mentioned earlier hangs suspended up in the air, invisibly held by divine command,
For King Mirian's men had been eager to raise up this glorious pillar, but being unable to raise it, they left it and went away, utterly without hope of raising it.
But through the prayer and supplication of our venerable mother Nino, the enlightener of the Georgians, it was suspended upright in the air by divine power, about one cubit [off the ground],
and it stands that way to this day, working many miracles and signs.
The blessed John came before this pillar and prayed to the Lord with tears, saying:
"Make known to me, O Lord, the way in which I should walk, and lead me by your truth to the place
where I may spend the rest of my life in quiet, in a way that pleases you. For by your will, O Sovereign, I have left the land that brought me forth and raised me.
So you, Steward of all, take care of my unworthiness and show me which way and where I should go to finish the course of this passing life."
And God, who does not disregard the supplication of his servants, showed him a mountain to the north of the city of Mtskheta and of the venerable Cross.
At once, bowing down again and giving thanks to Christ the Sovereign, he hurried up to the top of that mountain. When he saw it,
that it was suitable for living in solitude and free from all disturbance, he said to his disciples:
"My brothers, I will dwell here, for this pleases me, since it is good for us to be here."
They answered: "Venerable father, do as you say and as it pleases you."
So this turtledove, this lover of the desert, like another John the Forerunner in his other virtues, settled on the top of the mountain that had been shown to him.
He took up the hardest labours of the ascetic struggle: fasting, unceasing prayer, and standing upright,
which wholly withered and weakened the flesh. With a weak body he mightily resisted all the assaults and schemes of the deceiving devil.
For a body that has been weakened becomes strong in spirit, but one that pursues pleasures and delights weakens the soul and shows it to be wholly a slave of desires.
For this reason this divine man was eager to subdue the flesh by mortification and make it the slave and servant of the soul.
God settled on this mountain this ornament of the catholic Church, the great luminary of the people of Kartli,
so that from on high he might spread the brilliant lightning of his prayers over all the land around it.
And God sanctified that mountain through the prayer of that holy elder.
The multitude of demons that had dwelt there was driven from that place. Long ago the pagans had built a tower on that mountain, and an altar stood there,
on which godless men, wickedly led astray by the demons, performed abominable sacrifices to those most abominable demons.
But the abyss of mercy and goodness, through the sighs and supplications of the God-clad father John, drove out and expelled from that place those soul-slaying demons who deceive people.
And since he had always, from the very beginning, desired a life of quiet, for whose sake he had left his own land and gone beyond the borders of his homeland and his own place,
it pleased him to send out his disciples, as the apostles of Christ were once sent to preach to the gentiles the gospel of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.
So he spoke to them with sweet and fatherly words: "Children, why do you stand here and take no care for the benefit of others as well?
Or do you not know that our Lord Jesus Christ has sent us for the benefit of this land?

For, as you can see, this land is still a young plant. It needs to be watered with teachings, and the roots of its faith need to be enriched by preaching and by instruction like that of the holy apostles.
Therefore each of you should go and strengthen in the true faith those who have received baptism in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.
As for those who are still in ignorance and unbelief, teach them and make them disciples, so that they worship our Lord Jesus Christ.
Choose nothing above the love of God, and keep away from luxury and gluttony.
For it was through taste and food that Adam was driven out of the paradise of delight. By disobeying God's commandments he brought death upon his offspring, and many sweats,
struggles and labours he brought upon those who came after him, by tasting from the tree a single time.
Instead of deification he was condemned to death and exiled from paradise.
Yet Christ did not ignore how the devil oppressed in this way the one created by his own hands.
Instead, by becoming man and enduring painful sufferings as a man, he delivered us from the gates of death.
Although the wicked Satan deceitfully held out deification to the first father,
Christ truly made it share in divinity: God sharing in the human [?].
So you too should know, beloved, that through fasting, vigil, and keeping the body pure and undefiled, the soul that is cleansed of fleshly defilements becomes god and is united with God.
Flee wine entirely, for wine has no fellowship with ascetics, and still less with monks.
For wine binds those who take it without restraint with bonds that cannot be loosed, and like purchased slaves it hands them over dishonourably to the desires of sin.
Paul too called wine the root of evil when he said: "Do not get drunk with wine, from which comes debauchery."
Wine is also a deadly poison and the mother of evil desires.
My brothers, always remember death and keep that terrible day before the eyes of your mind, the day on which we must all stand there, naked and with downcast eyes.
Know, then, beloved, that this body is corruptible and passing away, and the soul alone will remain immortal. Let us struggle here, children.

Let us not spare ourselves, and let us not surrender our freedom to the passions. Let us endure pains that last a moment, for this is the time of affliction, but that eternal time is the time of rest.
Let us overcome our adversary here by fighting bravely, so that in the age to come we may receive crowns of victory.
Let us be on guard for that terrible hour when the soul is separated from these material bodies, for that hour is dreadful,
when the terrible heavenly hosts summon the soul to lead it to the place prepared for it, and to repay it according to its deeds, whether good or evil.
With these words, and with many more like them, the blessed father John, who instructed his disciples, sent them out to preach that the kingdom of heaven was near.
And they went on the way commanded to them, as men who had received authority to trample on snakes and scorpions and on all the power of the enemy.
And each of them went to the place where the Holy Spirit led them: some went toward Kakheti, while the venerable David came to the desert of Gareja.
And the blessed Isidore settled in the wooded valley of Samtavisi.
And Shio, clothed in God and a worker of wonders, found a small cave in the ravine of Mtskheta and shut himself away in it.
And the rest of them went to desert places, making their dwellings in the mountains and in caves and holes in the ground.
And all of these were martyred day after day for the faith, as the apostle says: destitute, afflicted, ill-treated, men of whom this world was not worthy,
since they had renounced all worldly cares. Most of them did not even own sheepskins or goatskins, and they judged themselves unworthy even of these;
instead, covered only by the skin they were born with, they endured the frosts of the night and the heat of the day. They remembered that the first parents too,
as long as they were naked because of their simplicity and their life without artifice, regarded their dwelling in paradise as the covering that wrapped them.
But when, through disobedience, they put on these coarse garments of skin, at the same time [they were cut off] from the tree of life and from paradise,
and exile from God befell them. Those who took this to heart were eager to enter paradise again through nakedness.
Such good workers, who were not hired for wages, were sent out by the blessed father John to that good work.
They had learned well from their teacher how to break up the ground of the souls of the faithful with the ploughs of teaching, and how to separate the wheat from the tares
that the envious enemy of mankind always sows in their minds by planting evil thoughts in human souls.
Certain God-loving believers in Christ came to these blessed fathers and learned from them the teaching of those in whom the Holy Spirit was present.
And others, who through ignorance were sick in two ways, in soul and in body, received healing once they came to knowledge through the teaching of these saints,
since God worked great healings and miracles through the prayers of these holy fathers, and these firmly strengthened the hearts of the faithful in the true faith.
And the demons were afraid. They left their places and fled to the deserts farther inland, and at the same time the idol shrines
were destroyed by those who had come to the knowledge of God through the teaching of the venerable fathers, and churches were built to glorify God.
Now the venerable John had with him relics of the holy martyrs, which he had brought from his own country,
and when he sent out his disciples, he gave each of them some of those holy relics,

so that they might have them as a guardian throughout their whole life against the wiles of the devils. And each took with him some of the relics of the saints, so that by looking on them he might always share in their martyrdom in his mind.
And they took them as their own treasure and wealth, and as a comfort in their life. These things, then, we have told about his disciples.
But our blessed father John stayed on that mountain and kept only one disciple with him, so that he might have him as a comfort in his weakness.
He himself gave himself over to the hard labours of ascetic struggle, and he never once rested from prayer and constant fasting.
By this he wore his flesh down completely and made it weak.
But his soul was strengthened, and his mind was cleansed of material things and of the strifes of the world. He held them on high before God, carrying out every form of ascetic struggle.
He completely forgot his body and counted the pleasures of the world as nothing, since they pass away and decay.
When those devils, the haters of good, saw him living in such ascetic struggle,
they were sawn apart with envy and, raging with fury, they were cut as if by a sword, for they could not bear to see the saint like this.
Then one day, clothed in utter shamelessness, they boldly attacked holy John. They frightened him greatly and showed fierce wrath and anger toward him.
They stood around him and raised a noisy uproar, letting out hideous cries, to frighten the elder and drive him away.
"Why," they said to him, "have you come to these places of ours, which we have held from the very beginning? What do you have to do with us, that you want to take our places by force?"
"So now, old man, if you do not leave this place willingly, we will bring many trials upon you. Then, forced against your will, you will learn not to seize other people's land."
But he sealed himself with the cross of Christ and said: "They surrounded me and closed me in,
and in the name of the Lord I drove them back. The Lord is my strength and my song, and he has become my salvation. I have trusted in God; I will not be afraid of what an enemy can do to me."
After this he turned to the devils and said: "Look, here I am."
"And if God has given you power over my body too, as he once did over Job,
do whatever you want. For I am a servant of my Lord Jesus Christ, and I am not afraid of your threats."
Then the chief of those devils called out angrily to the venerable John and said:
"John, John, why are you bothering us? Where have you come from, leaving your own place to come here?"
"So now go away from here quickly, for this place is ours, and you cannot live here with us."
"And if you do not listen to us," he said, "you will bring destruction on yourself, for you will not be able to stand against our strength and our numbers."
"So do not fool yourself. Go away from here to other places."
Then holy John answered those evil devils and said:
"You lovers of evil, you never want good things for our race, for you are schemers and liars."
And how should I listen to you, liars and vain ones, who never plan anything for the good of people, since you are eager to cast them down into hell?
And how can you tell me that this place is yours?
Is not the earth the Lord's, and its fullness, the world together with all who dwell in it, which he has granted to us people as a dwelling place?
But for you he has prepared the outer darkness and the unquenchable fire, in which you are destined to be punished forever, together with all who do your will.
And how can you advise me that it is better to leave this place, O deceiver, you who by guile and temptation drove our father Adam out of Paradise, you who stood in the way of his deification,
which we have now received through Christ Jesus? And now, see, you are driven out on every side by the descendants of Adam.
Therefore flee from here in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ and go far from this place, for Christ has granted it to me.
When Saint John had said this, at once all those demons together let out a cry of woe and said, lamenting:
"Woe to us, for you have come! By the invoking of the name of Jesus we are driven out of every place, and we are seen defeated even by those who follow him, for he grants them victory over us.
Come, let us flee from here and go away to the more remote pagans and dwell among them."
And immediately, as they spoke, something like a dark mist came out of the mountain and moved off toward the north, and from then on all the demons vanished from that place and went away.
And when all who lived around that mountain heard what God had done, and how the demons had been driven out by the prayer of Saint John,
they all gave glory to God, for they knew the wickedness of those demons who had dwelt on that mountain,
since those evil spirits had inflicted many sufferings on their neighbors. For this reason all who lived round about were amazed at these miracles and, struck with awe, said:
"Truly God is wonderful among his saints, who does the will of those who fear him, and blessed is his holy name forever."
With such graces and signs this venerable father of ours shone, and he was enriched with every virtue,
for at all times, with an ever-watchful mind and a vigilant soul, he went around among his disciples, so that he would not find any of them slackened by negligence and unprepared for that unknown day
on which the Bridegroom, when he comes, calls the purified souls that are prepared and adorned to enter the heavenly bridal chamber.
Therefore he added fasts to fasting, and to prayer further supplications and psalmody.
Now the mountain on which this sign-clad man lived was at first without water. And when he saw the hard labor and the sweat of his disciple,
which he endured in fetching water, for he would take up a water jar and go down to the foot of that mountain and from there bring up water for the elder's use, the elder took pity on him.
And with tears he begged God that he who had made water flow for Israel in the wilderness from the hard rock would also make a spring rise up for them here on that mountain, as a comfort to them.
And God heard the entreaty of his servant, and on that dry, waterless ground, or rather upon the rock, sweet and pleasant-tasting water sprang up for him,
which still springs up abundantly to this day, to the glory of God and of his servant John.
And when this miracle became known to the neighbours and to those who lived around that mountain, how water had sprung up on that mountain through the prayer of that holy man,
for all of them knew that it had been dry and waterless before, they therefore came to him from every side, carrying the sick and those gripped by any kind of suffering.
And when they drank of that water and let it drip onto any wound, they at once obtained healing. And to this day,
for those who take of this water with faith, it becomes a benefit to them through the prayer of the holy father John.
But the venerable John did not wish to build on that place; instead, having found a small cave on that mountain, he ended his life there.
And through performing many miracles he shone forth like the sun.
And the report of him spread through all the land of Kartli.
For the countless abundance of graces and his wonder-working deeds made them known to all,
since this is how God knows to glorify those who glorify him: through a multitude of powers and signs.
Now one day a disciple of this venerable man once went to the spring that had sprung up through the holy man's prayer.
And as he drew near, he saw that a very large bear was standing at it.
And in fear he ran as fast as he could to the elder and told him about the bear he had seen at the spring.
And the elder rose and followed his disciple to the spring, and when he saw the bear he spoke to it gently:
"Drink, if you are thirsty, and go away. But I tell you: from now on do not harm any of the people who live on this mountain, not a single one."
When the bear heard these words from the elder, it went away with head bowed and quietly, like an obedient servant who had been rebuked [?] by the venerable man.
In this way this good lawgiver knew how to lay down the law even for dumb animals,
for from that time to this day the dumb kind of these beasts has kept the holy man's command in this way, so that if any of them encounter anyone on this mountain,
they at once fulfil what the holy man ordered, and turn straight back toward another place and go on their way without doing any harm to people.
This miracle greatly surpasses that of Daniel, for he by prayer kept only himself unharmed by the lions, and that only at the time, and only from those shut up with him in the pit.
But this great and wonderful father taught even the offspring of the bear he had seen, just as he had taught the first one, not only not to harm him,
but not to harm anyone else at all among the people walking on that mountain. The bears of this mountain keep this command to this very day.
Once some people brought to this wonder-working father John a paralysed man who had lost the use of all his limbs. He was a pitiful sight to the eyes of those who saw him.
They laid him, stretched out on a litter, before the holy man, and the paralysed man's relatives spoke to the blessed one with lamentation:

"Have mercy on this paralytic, holy one of God, for we believe that through your prayer to God you are able to do all things, as one who does the will of our Lord Jesus Christ and is his faithful servant."
And the paralytic himself cried out just as loudly, in a pitiful voice, as far as he was able, if any power of speech was left in him at all:
"Have mercy on me, servant of the merciful God, on this dead man who has not yet been given to the grave, and pray to God for me, so that I may be healed through your prayer."
Though the matter seemed hard to the blessed John, his soul was moved with pity for the wretched paralytic. He rose to pray and begged God to heal the man who was gripped by this evil affliction.
After this he turned to him and said, just as the Lord himself once said to the paralytic at the pool by the Sheep Gate:
"Rise, take up your bed," for our Lord Jesus Christ heals you.
O your wonders, Christ! The man who had been half dead and given up as completely lost rose at once to his feet and stood before the elder, healed in all his limbs.
Everyone gathered there saw this glorious deed, and in amazement they glorified God, who works such miracles through his servant.
And those who heard of and saw these great wonders were strengthened in faith in the Holy Trinity.
Another time they brought to this holy man a certain man in whom a demon of muteness had taken up residence. He was severely tormented by that evil spirit and could not speak at all.
When holy John saw him, he took pity on him and said to the demon that was living in this man:
"Evil and wicked spirit, why do you torment God's creature? I tell you in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ: come out of that man and go away to desert and pathless places."
At once, at the elder's command, the demon came out of the man and left him healed. All who saw it marveled, and in awe they said:
"Who is this, who drives out demons with a word and quickly grants healing to the sick?" But the blessed John said to them:
"Do not be amazed, O people, at the mighty works of God, for it is not I who heal, but the invocation of the name of our Lord Jesus Christ,
which drives out demons and banishes people's diseases and infirmities, and every power of the deceiving devil comes to nothing. For he himself declared:
'Whoever believes in me will also do the works that I do, and will do greater works than mine.' And he is the healer of all and the worker of wonders."
With such graces the blessed John shone, and God adorned him with such miracles.
For he performed countless mighty works and signs on earth.
There are many miracles that he performed in the land of Assyria, and it is impossible to mention each one because it would take too long.
We have related these few of his wonders to show what kind of man this God-clothed father was.
Since his flesh had been worn down by fasting and constant prayer,
And he had grown weak in every way, having reached a good old age and having taken on many struggles in the cave mentioned above.
It was fitting that he too should rest from such great labors and receive the reward for his sweat and struggles.
For he had given up everything he had, and above all his own body, to the service of God, his Lord. Because of this he had gathered great wealth in the treasuries of heaven.
So, knowing through the Holy Spirit that the time of his death had come, he called some of his disciples, along with Elias the deacon and Tatas,
who had built a monastery below that mountain and lived in it with many brothers whom he had gathered into that monastery.
And he said to them: "My children, the time of my end has come, and I know that I am departing from this body. So I am very much afraid
that the band of evil adversaries, the guardians of the air, those bitter ones who are quick to cast the human race down into the depths of hell, may become hinderers to me."
"Now then, my brothers, you too must always expect death and guard yourselves well against the snares of the devil,
so that our evil enemy, who watches the [?] of our soul day after day, does not become a stumbling stone for you."
"And who is able to be delivered from their hands, unless he receives power from God through fasting and purity of body?"
"For this reason I beg you, my children, to be watchful at all times and to serve the Lord in purity. And remember me too in your prayers."
Behold the meekness and humility of that blameless soul! For while he was still in the body, the utterly dreadful demons appeared to him, and he drove them away with a word.

And now he was leaving the body completely and standing before the royal thrones through the purification of his soul and mind, and he had received the grace of foreknowledge from the divine and Holy Spirit.
Even so, out of surpassing humility, he judged himself unworthy and feared the spirits who guard the air.
For he had learned from Paul, the mouth of Christ, not to speak boastfully but to say humbly, like this:
"I have done what I was obliged to do, and as for the rest, I am an unprofitable servant of my Lord."
After he had taught his disciples in this way, he also instructed them to lay his body in the same place where he had lived as a stranger.
After this he received the incorruptible and immortal mysteries of Christ. Lifting up his eyes, he seemed to be looking joyfully at certain beings toward whom he turned.
He was looking with his eyes because the host of the bodiless ones of heaven had been sent, so that the Lord might glorify His servant, who had glorified Him on earth in weak flesh.
A little later he gave up his spirit to the angels, to be brought to his Lord,
who called him to the resting places of heaven in return for the labors and pains he had taken on himself on earth.
His disciples fell at his feet, bathed them with tears and wept bitterly, as people left orphans by such a father. With words like these they said:
"Honored father and laborer for souls, where will we see an angelic face from now on? Or who will be the healer of the twofold weakness of human beings,
Or who will raise up those who have fallen in mind, and where will people find a remedy against demons? Who is like you!
They drenched the floor with holy tears. They said these things and many more like them, as was fitting for souls deprived of such a treasure.
But they disregarded the word the elder had given them about his body. He had told his disciples where to lay his flesh, but they thought that place unworthy of one so wholly worthy.
Priests and deacons came, with a very great crowd of people. Those who wrapped his body reverently carried it away to the monastery built by Tata, his disciple.
They made a sarcophagus and reverently placed his precious relics in it. Then they kissed his tomb and quickly departed.
But John, great among the fathers, would not tolerate the disregard of his word. Truly living even after death, he wished
his relics to be laid in the same place where he had struggled while still in the flesh and had finished this course of ascetic struggle.
So great earthquakes took place in that spot. They made it plain that the saint of God wanted to go back to his former dwelling-place.
Then his disciples remembered the elder's word. They told the catholicos and the whole body of the church what the venerable one had commanded them.
When the catholicos heard this, he went with priests and deacons.

With great honour, with the people going before them, with a multitude of candles and with hymns of praise, they carried his body, which had struggled so much, up to the cave mentioned earlier. There they laid it with loving honour.
After his relics had been carried up, the earthquake at Tata's monastery stopped.
Many other miracles also took place when his relics were carried up. Many sick people, held by diseases of every kind, were healed just by touching this holy body.
And if anyone comes to his tomb with faith, whatever illness grips him, he quickly finds healing from the disease that afflicts him.
A long time afterwards, the holy Clement, catholicos of Mtskheta, built another church on the east side of this cave
in the name of Saint John the Baptist, to the glory of God and of his servant, our blessed father John.
Shining with such graces, the all-praised John brought glory to the land of the Georgians and taught it the whole service of God.
He did this not only by himself but also through his disciples. One of his disciples built the church of Alaverdi, dedicated to the renowned martyr George,
and he worked many miracles, as his teacher also had.
Another disciple prepared the cave of Iulti as a dwelling for God's ascetics and monks.
One of them built a monastery in Zena Sopeli, which no female creature enters, and where no bird dares to nest.
Others again built monasteries in Kakheti and greatly increased the faith. The Lord had appointed them as preachers and to teach the knowledge of God to those who did not know it.

Such were the struggles and labours of this man of God, which he endured for God's sake. Likewise, while he was still in the flesh, he received fitting rewards for them, being adorned with miracles and signs.
After he left the body and passed from this world, he made his dwelling in the heavenly tabernacles and bridal chambers. There he delights in unceasing delights and sees the light
of divine glory, which never grows dark. He rejoices in the indescribable good things which eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor have they entered into the heart of man.
He rejoices, placed in the ranks of the fathers, and exults with the choir of angels, singing with festive voices.
For he passed through fire and water, enduring many struggles in this visible world that we perceive with the senses. What else was due to him,
except that he should go up to rest in those invisible dwellings that are known only to the mind?

O father of fathers and glory of monks, who appeared as the pride of the Georgian people, truly worthy to dwell in the blessedness of heaven, thrice-blessed one, ornament of those who live under a monastic rule:
look down from the vaults of heaven upon us, your unworthy children, who are harshly oppressed by our most wicked enemies who hate mankind, the demons.
Standing before the throne of the Holy Trinity of threefold light, plead for us to be set free from the tyranny of the flesh and the passions,
so that, once freed from the evil thoughts of the heart that trouble us so greatly, we may find some proper peace and leisure.
And so, with a purified mind, may we be made worthy to offer thanks and praise to the Father, who has no beginning, and to his only-begotten
Son, who like him has no beginning, together with the all-holy and life-giving Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
